final_message:
I built the Ploverdesk landing page in React, Vite and plain CSS, but I could not build it or look at it: this sandbox has no `node`, so `npm run build` (including the `tsc` type check) was never run. Nothing was rendered either: no dev server and no browser, so the page has never been viewed. Nobody was there to answer, so every decision below is my own and nothing was validated.

**What's on the page**
- **Header:** the Ploverdesk name, a quiet "Book a demo" link (`/demo`) and a "Start trial" button (`/trial`).
- **Opening screen:** the headline "Pay the invoices that match. Look only at the lines that do not.", a short paragraph, both actions, and "14-day trial. No credit card." Below that is an example table labelled "Example", comparing one supplier invoice with its purchase order and delivery note:
  - one grey row for the lines that agree, marked "To payment approval";
  - three rows for the brief's mismatches (wrong quantity, wrong unit price, delivery never arrived), with the document that disagrees flagged in burnt orange.

  It contains no figures, only the brief's words.
- **"From the inbox to your accounting system":** a short spec list covering input, the three-way match, review, approval, export (CSV or API) and hosting in Frankfurt.
- **Price:** 290 EUR per month per company, no limit on users, the trial needs no credit card, then both actions again.
- **Footer:** "Founded in 2025. We are six people in Rotterdam."

No logos, testimonials, quotes or other figures were invented.

**Look and motion**
- White page, near-black text, thin grey rules.
- The only colour is the orange that marks a mismatch. The trial button is black, so the colour never doubles as the call to action.
- The system font, two weights, square corners, no shadows. No web font, because none can be loaded offline.
- Hover changes colour in 150ms. There is no scroll animation.
- The one motion: half a second after the page loads, the "agrees" row fades from black to grey over 400ms, the way the product sets matched lines aside. It is grey from the start if the animation doesn't run or the visitor has asked for reduced motion.
- On narrow phones, each table row becomes a stacked block with every value next to its document name. Below 30rem the header drops its demo link, which still appears just below in the opening screen.

**Files**
- `src/App.tsx`, `src/index.css` and `src/tokens.css` (new; every value comes from `MASTER.md`)
- `index.html` (new title and description)
- `MASTER.md`, the design system
- `preview/thesis.html` and `preview/design-system.html`, throwaway previews

**Static audit**
- **Two layout problems found and fixed:**
  - On a short wide screen the last table row sat at the fold, so the headline was widened to fit on two lines.
  - The table's wrapper kept the browser's default 40px side margins, which pushed it off the shared left edge.
- **One check still flags:** it reports `.button:hover` and `.link:hover` as having no transition. The transitions are on the base rules (`src/index.css:84` and `:109`) and the hover rules sit inside a hover-capable-device query, so I don't think it's a real problem.
- **Passed:**
  - 27 other code checks found nothing: no layout properties animated, focus outlines intact, reduced motion handled, no looping animation, one label per action, no invented figures, no em dashes.
  - Colour contrast is computed, not eyeballed: body text 17.8:1, secondary text 7.9:1, grey rows 5.3:1, flagged mismatch text 6.1:1 on its background.
- **No disabled state in use:** the page has no disabled controls; the disabled style exists but nothing uses it.

**Left unverified**
- `npm run build` and `tsc --noEmit`.
- The layout at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px. In particular, the claim that the whole table is visible without scrolling at about 1440×800 is a size estimate, not a check.
- Smoothness of the one animation, checked in a browser's performance tools.
- The page with the system's "reduce motion" setting turned on.
- Whether the narrow-screen table is still read as a table by screen readers.

A multi-agent pipeline (bunshin) exists for whole sites, but this was a single page, so I didn't use it.

Modules loaded: tells, ui-ux-pro-max, motion-principles, css-native, mobile-principles, design-audit
Modules not loaded: none

How did it come out? One minute, and plain or wrong counts as much as good:
